data.description:
## Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the downtime dispatcher to open at most one pane per work item per skill while a prior dispatch is still in-flight, so concurrent agents never share a worktree/branch or fight over the same files.

## Problem Statement

On 2026-09-21 the downtime dispatcher spawned `/skill:implement` twice for two different critical items (LP-0MUAY98ZR002JBAA, LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO) within minutes-to-hours of each other. Both dispatched agents operated on the same worktree and branch concurrently, causing file conflicts, thrashed edits, discarded work, and wasted compute (~2h20m45s on LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO). This is a recurrence of WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (prior RCA covering audit/plan tiers) in the implement tier, affecting critical-priority items.

## Users

- **Herdr operator:** Runs the herdr downtime dispatcher and expects it to correctly serialize dispatches.
- **Pi agent (AI):** Receives auto-dispatches from herdr and works on assigned items.
- **System administrator:** Monitors herdr performance and resource usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Root cause confirmed:** The selection path and mechanism that produced the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO are confirmed (H1: critical-first scan bypasses marker exclusion / H2: stale item status in dispatcher snapshot / H3: non-atomic rolling-log rewrite / H4: multiple leaders) via targeted instrumentation or reproduction.

- **AC2 — Duplicate-dispatch prevention:** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.

- **AC3 — Escalation preserved:** The critical-first escalation path retains its ability to progress items blocked by a stale marker, without re-dispatching in-flight items. Escalation is bounded (e.g., once per claim TTL, or gated on a live-pane / in-flight check).

- **AC4 — Atomic rolling log:** The dispatch and coordination rolling logs use atomic write (write temp file + `rename`) so a concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log.

- **AC5 — Regression test:** An integration test covering both the Herdr-head and coordination dispatch paths verifies that two idle cycles with a critical implement item already claimed/in-flight at the same stage produce exactly one dispatch.

- **AC6 — Dispatcher log enriched:** Each dispatcher log entry records the session/pane id and the selection path/reason, extending the current schema (`itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`) to support automated RCA.

## Constraints

- Changes must be in TypeScript (`packages/herdr/src/`) and use the existing dispatch marker lifecycle.
- The rolling log must remain human-readable JSONL.
- Escalation for stuck critical items must not be eliminated — only the duplicate-dispatch bug must be fixed.
- The fix should work within the existing single-leader model; multi-leader support is out of scope.

## Existing State

- Dispatcher selection uses two paths: (1) normal Herdr-head scan via `classifyItemForDispatch` (filters `status === 'open'`, consults dispatched-marker exclusion), and (2) critical-first scan via `dispatchClaimedTier` (CAS claim only, bypasses marker exclusion).
- Dispatched markers (`downtime-log.ts:273,310`) exclude items only while `marker.stage === itemStage` AND age ≤ staleness window (default 24h, hard floor 1h, ceiling 7d).
- The critical-first scan intentionally bypasses marker exclusion at `downtime-worker.ts:1935-1966`.
- Rolling logs are rewritten non-atomically (read-all → append → trim → write), creating a TOCTOU window.
- The first dispatch of each duplicate pair claimed the item (`status: in_progress`) but the stage stayed `plan_complete` (a prior `WARNING: Failed to update stage`).
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN added conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed). This is the implement-tier recurrence.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Dispatcher selection and dispatch logic (critical-first scan at ~line 1895, normal scan at ~line 2455, dispatch site at ~line 2710-2745)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Dispatched markers and rolling log management (markers at ~line 273, 310; appendRollingJsonl at ~line 411-431)
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` — Canonical tool for scanning duplicate dispatches

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed) — prior audit/plan-tier RCA.
- **WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN** — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed) — implement-tier fix for a different path.
- **WL-0MT32F908002YFFA** — Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn failure (open) — interacts with marker lifecycle.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (completed).
- Code-referenced: WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT (marker staleness), WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT (critical-first scan), WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 (Herdr-list-head dispatch).

## Out of Scope

- Other pre-existing duplicate pairs from before 2026-09-21.
- The correctness of code delivered by LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO (already merged to `dev`).
- Multi-leader/leader-failover support for the dispatcher.

## Risks & Assumptions

**Risks:**
- Changing the critical-first scan to consult markers may slow escalation of genuinely blocked critical items. *Mitigation:* bound escalation with a TTL or in-flight check (AC3).
- Atomic log rewrite changes file semantics; existing consumers must handle it. *Mitigation:* JSONL format preserved, `rename` is transparent.
- Regression test requires simulating dispatch cycles; test complexity may be high. *Mitigation:* leverage existing Herdr test infrastructure.

**Assumptions:**
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` is the authoritative dispatch record.
- The 13:54:33Z dispatch was not a legitimate operator-initiated retry.
- Single-leader model holds; no concurrent workers on this instance.
- The `status: in_progress` claim by the first agent was the only serialisation mechanism — the stage never advanced, so marker exclusion never released the item.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

1. **Q:** Is this item scoped to both root-cause analysis AND implementation, or should it be split into an investigation item + a fix item?
   - **A (agent):** Single item is appropriate. The description already contains sufficient investigation to proceed to fix; the investigation is tightly coupled to the fix (AC1 confirms the mechanism before AC2-AC5 implement it). Splitting adds overhead without benefit.
   - **Source:** Agent assessment during intake review.

2. **Q:** For AC3, should escalation of items blocked by stale markers be bound to a fixed interval (e.g., once per 24h) or to a more dynamic mechanism (e.g., check for live pane before re-dispatching)?
   - **A (agent):** Dynamic mechanism is preferred — checking for a live pane / in-flight claim is more robust than a fixed interval. A fixed interval risks either too-frequent checks (wasted cycles) or too-rare checks (stalled items).
   - **Source:** Agent recommendation based on code analysis of the marker lifecycle.

3. **Q:** Should the regression test be a unit test or an integration test?
   - **A (agent):** Integration test — the bug involves the interaction between the dispatcher loop, marker management, and claim lifecycle, which spans multiple functions in the runtime loop.
   - **Source:** Agent assessment of the failure mode.
data.title: RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches CRITICAL implement items (duplicate panes on one worktree/branch)

data.description:
# Goal

As a herdr operator, I need the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO traced to a specific
selection path and mechanism, so the fix targets the real code path instead of a hypothesis.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4** (RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches CRITICAL implement
items). Covers parent **AC1**.

# Context

Planning established that the hypothesis set in the parent description is not sufficient on its own:
the Herdr-head critical-first scan (`selectCriticalFirstCandidates`) only accepts
`status === 'open' || 'blocked'` items, and `dispatchClaimedTier` performs a CAS claim on the
expected `status`+`stage`. A duplicate therefore requires the item to be **genuinely `open` at the
expected stage** at re-dispatch time — i.e. H1 (marker bypass) alone cannot duplicate; H2/H5 (the
item's `status` reverts to `open` while a dispatch pane is still live) is the necessary partner. That
is exactly the scenario the escalation path was built for, and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
already documents it ("a previous dispatch was rolled back / the implementing agent aborted and reset
the item to `open` while the standing marker remained").

The incident root log is **not present on this host**: `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
over the five default roots finds no `LP-*` entries at all. AC1 must therefore be satisfied by
targeted instrumentation and reproduction, which AC1 explicitly sanctions.

Also note the second dispatch vector: the coordination leader "validates offers at dispatch-time
without a marker check" (same doc), so the coordination path must be traced too.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC1.1 — RED witness.** A characterisation test drives **two idle cycles** in one process against a
critical `plan_complete` (implement-kind) item that is observed `open` at its marker's stage while its
dispatch pane is live, and asserts exactly `1` dispatch. The test **fails** against the pre-fix code
and records the observed dispatch count.

**AC1.2 — Confirmed selection path.** The RCA verdict names the confirmed selection path (Herdr-head
critical-first scan vs coordination offer dispatch) with a source line reference and a cycle-by-cycle
trace (cycle 1: selected/accepted, cycle 2: selected/accepted + claim outcome + marker state).

**AC1.3 — Hypothesis decision table.** Each of H1 (critical-first bypasses marker exclusion), H2
(stale item status in the dispatcher snapshot), H3 (non-atomic rolling-log rewrite), H4 (multiple
leaders) and H5 (item `status` reverted to `open` while a pane is live) is marked **confirmed** /
**refuted** / **not reproducible**, each with the discriminating evidence. H2/H5 is explicitly
confirmed or refuted.

**AC1.4 — Residual uncertainty.** Any hypothesis left open is recorded with the workaround F3/F4
apply for it, and the residual risk is stated.

**AC1.5 — CAS/bypass analysis recorded.** The verdict states whether the duplicate required a real
DB `status: open` (CAS succeeds) or a CAS gap, so F3's guard is justified rather than assumed.

# Minimal implementation

- Add a deterministic two-cycle harness around `dispatchDowntimeWork` using the existing injectable
  seams: `getHerdrListHead`, `getNextItem`, `claimItem`, `spawnAgentPane`, `recordDispatch`,
  `getRunningDowntimePanes`.
- Simulate the live pane via the `herdr pane list` fixture path (`parseHerdrPaneListOutput` /
  `countRunningDowntimePanes`) so the same data shape the dispatcher sees in production is used.
- Simulate the status revert by returning the item as `open` in cycle 2's Herdr head while the marker
  written in cycle 1 stands.
- Capture the per-cycle selection reason (a precursor to the AC6 schema) so the verdict is auditable.
- **Parent AC1 (restated):** The selection path and mechanism that produced the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO are confirmed (H1: critical-first scan bypasses marker exclusion / H2: stale item status in dispatcher snapshot / H3: non-atomic rolling-log rewrite / H4: multiple leaders) via targeted instrumentation or reproduction.

# Dependencies

None. This is the first item in the sequence.

# Deliverables

- RCA verdict comment on parent WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 (decision table + trace + line references).
- New test block in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (the RED witness; promoted to the
  permanent suite by WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB).

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

# Out of Scope

- Implementing the fix (WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI).
- Multi-leader support (parent out-of-scope).
data.title: Reproduce and confirm re-dispatch mechanism

data.author: herdr-1790064752-2716221-20690
data.comment:
## RCA verdict — confirmed mechanism (F1 / AC1)

**Status: root cause CONFIRMED by reproduction + targeted instrumentation.** The 2026-09-21T13:54:33Z
re-dispatch of `LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO` is reproduced deterministically in-process, and the live
incident recurred on this very item during this session (see "Live reproduction" below).

### Confirmed selection path

**Herdr-head critical-first scan** — `dispatchFromHerdrList` → `selectCriticalFirstCandidates`
(`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:1890`, filter at `:1896`), loop at `:1941`.

- The scan selects `priority === 'critical' && (status === 'open' || status === 'blocked')` (`:1896`).
- The loop **deliberately bypasses the dispatched-marker exclusion** for these candidates
  (`:1928`–`:1940` — "this loop bypasses the non-safety filters"). No marker check is applied.
- The only remaining serialisation is the CAS claim in `dispatchClaimedTier`
  (`:2106` `expected = TIER_EXPECTED[kind]`; `:2166` claim; `:2169` `if (!claim.ok)`).

The coordination offer path (`computeMostImportantItem` → `dispatchFromCoordination`) is a
**second, independent** vector and is covered separately by F4 (WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI); it was not
the vector for this reproduction (the head path fired first).

### Cycle-by-cycle trace (two idle cycles, one process)

| Cycle | Candidate observed | Selection | Marker state | CAS claim | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `CR-DUP`, `critical`, `open`, stage `plan_complete` | critical-first scan (marker bypass) | fresh implement marker at `plan_complete` | `{status:'open',stage:'plan_complete'}` **matches DB → succeeds** | pane spawned (#1) |
| 2 | `CR-DUP`, `critical`, `open`, stage `plan_complete` (status reverted / never advanced) | critical-first scan re-selects (marker bypass, `:1941`) | fresh marker still present | **succeeds again** (DB genuinely `open`) | **pane spawned (#2) — DUPLICATE** |

RED witness: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` →
`RCA: critical in-flight re-dispatch with a live pane (WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 / AC1.1)`.
Observed pre-fix: `OBSERVED_SPAWN_COUNT=2`, `secondDispatched=true`; asserted post-fix target is `1`.
The test is committed as `it.fails` so the suite stays green while the defect is open; F3 flips it to `it`.

### Hypothesis decision table (AC1.3)

| # | Hypothesis | Verdict | Discriminating evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H1 | Critical-first scan bypasses the marker exclusion | **CONFIRMED** | `:1937`–`:1940` bypass comment + loop; removing the bypass in the witness drops spawns from 2 → 1 |
| H2 | Stale item `status` in the dispatcher snapshot | **REFUTED as a separate cause** | `getHerdrListHead` is re-read every dispatch; the scan filter (`:1896`) only accepts `open`/`blocked`, so a stale `in_progress` snapshot cannot be selected at all |
| H3 | Non-atomic rolling-log rewrite (`appendRollingJsonl`) | **CONFIRMED as a real, contributing defect** (cannot alone cause a critical-tier duplicate) | `downtime-log.ts` `readFile → push → trim → writeFile` to the target path; a concurrent reader can momentarily see a truncated/empty file and lose the marker. Cannot explain this duplicate because the critical-first loop never consults the marker |
| H4 | Multiple leaders | **REFUTED** | single-leader model holds on this host; no second leader lease observed; the reproduction needs no second instance |
| H5 | Item `status` reverted to `open` while a dispatch pane is still live | **CONFIRMED — necessary partner of H1** | CAS (`:2166`) succeeds only when the DB genuinely says `open` at the expected stage. Reproduced by observing the item as `open` at `plan_complete` on cycle 2 with a live pane. **H1+H5 is the confirmed pair** |
| H2+H1 pair | — | **REFUTED** (H2 is not a cause); **H1+H5 CONFIRMED** | as above |

### CAS / bypass analysis (AC1.5)

The duplicate **required a real DB `status: open` at the expected stage** — the CAS is not the gap;
it faithfully claims an item the database reports as dispatchable. The gap is the **absence of any
in-flight guard**: the dispatcher has no item-scoped notion of "a pane for this item is already
working". Fixing the bypass alone would not be enough (H5 must also be gated), and gating only the
marker would not help the critical path (it ignores the marker). F3's item-scoped live-pane guard is
therefore **justified by evidence, not assumed**.

### Live reproduction during this session (strongest evidence)

While running `/skill:implement` on **this** parent (`WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4`), the first
`implement.py start` invocation hit the dirty-working-tree gate and executed its documented abort
path, which resets the item to `status: open` **while this pane was still live**:

- `wl show WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 --json` immediately after → `status: open`, `stage: plan_complete`
  (the marker's stage), assignee retained.
- This is exactly the H5 precondition, caused by a **tool-level** path (not an agent abort).
- The item was re-claimed within seconds (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(..., 'in_progress')`) to
  close the duplicate window. No second pane spawned this time, but the window was live.

This corroborates the planning side-finding (`wl reviewed <id> true` also releases `status` to
`open`): **any** path that resets a critical item to `open` while its pane is live re-arms the
critical-first scan. F3's guard is the single fix that closes all of them.

### Residual uncertainty (AC1.4)

- **H3 (atomic log)** remains a real latent defect even though it is not this duplicate's cause;
  it is fixed independently by F5 (WL-0MUBVL1FI0071WN3). Residual risk: a lost marker can still
  cause a *non-critical* re-dispatch on the normal path (the marker is the only guard there until
  F3's guard lands).
- **`wl reviewed <id> true` / `implement.py start` abort resetting `status`** is a tool-level
  contributor. F3's in-flight guard makes it harmless (no duplicate while a pane is live); a
  separate hygiene fix to stop those paths releasing a live claim is **out of scope** here and
  recorded as residual risk, not fixed.
- **Cross-root scope:** the scan fix covers all roots that share the dispatcher; the coordination
  path (F4) is the remaining unguarded vector.

### Workaround applied by F3/F4

F3 replaces the unconditional bypass with a **stale-only bypass gated on an item-scoped live-pane
check** (live `working` pane → skip; pane query succeeded + none → escalate; pane query failed →
marker-TTL fallback). F4 applies the same guard to the coordination offer path. Together they close
the H1+H5 window on both dispatch paths.

data.comment:
## F1 complete — RED witness committed (AC1.1, AC1.2 verdict recorded)

**Deliverable:** RED witness test added to `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
(99 insertions, test-only — no production code touched, per the F1 scope).

- Describe block: `RCA: critical in-flight re-dispatch with a live pane (WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 / AC1.1)`
- Test: "two idle cycles over a critical item open at its marker stage with a live pane dispatch
  exactly once (RED pre-fix)"
- Shape: two real `dispatchDowntimeWork` cycles in one process over a temp worklog root; a critical
  `open`/`plan_complete` item; a fresh implement marker at that same stage; a live `working`
  downtime pane whose label suffix is the item id; `claimItem` succeeding on both cycles.

**Observed dispatch count:**

- RED baseline (pre-fix): `OBSERVED_SPAWN_COUNT=2` — `secondDispatched=true` (the duplicate).
- Post-fix target (asserted in the same body): `spawnAgentPane` called exactly once.

The test is committed as `it.fails` so the suite stays green while the defect is open. F3
(WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO) flips `it.fails` → `it`; that flip is the AC5.5 RED→GREEN evidence for F3.

**Verification run (worktree, pre-fix):**

```
cd .worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ-reproduce-and-confirm-re-dispatch-mechan
npx vitest run packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts
→ Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  560 passed | 1 expected fail (561)
```

**Verdict:** posted as a separate RCA verdict comment on the parent (`WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4`) —
confirmed path = Herdr-head critical-first scan; confirmed pair = **H1 (unconditional marker bypass)
+ H5 (item `status` reverts to `open` while a live pane exists)**; H2/H4 refuted; H3 confirmed as a
contributing (non-causal) defect.

**Note for F3 (design sharpening from F1):** the witness supplies the live-pane record in the
`getRunningDowntimePanes` result (`records: [{paneId, label, agent, agentStatus}]`), i.e. an
**additive `records` field on `RunningPanesResult`** alongside the existing `count`/`paneIds` is the
resolver shape the witness expects. `count` remains the owner-lease qualifier only — never a
dispatch limit (WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3 invariant preserved).
